Hi Tara / Rajiv,

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. As discussed, we want to kick off a short Sprint 0 MAP to align stakeholders and lock the evaluation & close timeline for NovusData's private deployment. Goal is to confirm network/VPN and IAM/KMS ownership and produce an agreed checklist for the evaluation window (2 weeks).

Quick objectives for Sprint 0 (proposal):
- Confirm network topology and VPN handoff point (NovusData infra owner)
- Identify IAM and KMS contacts + access cadence for test deployment
- Share a minimal network diagram and preflight checklist we can use for the evaluation
- Confirm evaluation dates and success criteria so Redwood can provision private test capacity

Who I’ve looped in from Redwood: Camila (Account Exec / commercial), Marcus (Solutions — infra + deployment), Hannah (On‑prem / private packager), Mateo (Networking). Please reply with who from Novus should own network config set-up and the contact for key management / security integration.

I attached a proposed MAP timeline and a draft network diagram to get us started. Proposed evaluation window: Jun 1 — Jun 14, 2026. If that works we'll finalize the MAP and schedule a 30m handoff next week.

Next steps (ask to Novus):
1) Confirm network owner (VPN / peering) + best contact for scheduling a connectivity test
2) Confirm IAM/KMS owner and whether you're using an external HSM or cloud KMS (and which provider)
3) Share any blocker windows (maintenance, procurement, security approvals) in the next 48 hours

Thanks — happy to adjust timeline based on your inputs.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Kimberly — thanks for the clear note. We can move forward with the proposed window. Confirming owners from our side:
- Network / VPN owner: Rajiv Singh (cc’d) — network lead, will own VPN handoff and connectivity test scheduling.
- IAM / KMS owner: Tara Wong (me) — I’ll coordinate with our Security Architect but we’re planning to use AWS KMS (symmetric keys) for this PoC; if Redwood requires HSM-backed keys we’ll need to validate procurement timing.

We’ll do an internal pre-check and get the network diagram feedback to you by EOD tomorrow. Two quick asks from us to Redwood before the handoff:
1) A short list of required firewall ports and IP ranges for the private test cluster
2) A sample IAM role policy for the deployment agent (so our security team can pre-authorize it)

If those are available in a short doc we can close Sprint 0 rapid.

Tara

Thanks Tara — quick reply from the infra side with the checklist items we typically hand to customers for Sprint 0 connectivity prep. Attaching a condensed checklist here and pasting the essentials below so your security team can triage quickly.

Essentials we need from Novus before we provision the private test:
- Public egress IP ranges (or CIDR) that the private cluster will use for control plane callbacks
- Allowed inbound ports: 22 (jumpbox admin, optional), 443 (API / TLS), 5222 (agent), 500/4500 UDP if using IPsec for site-to-site VPN; we can support AWS Transit Gateway or customer terminator IPsec
- VPN handoff: preferred is customer-terminator with static public IP; we also support AWS side termination if you prefer
- A temporary IAM role ARN and trust policy for the deployment agent (we’ll only request least-privilege for provisioning)
- KMS: if using AWS KMS provide key ARN and whether key policy permits Redwood service principal; if HSM, list vendor and provisioning window

If you want I can run a connectivity test script during the initial window — Rajiv, if you can provision a BGP-less static IP tunnel or a test peer for the week of May 25 we’ll validate end-to-end before Jun 1.

I attached rdw-network-diagram-draft.png and a condensed checklist file.

Cheers,
Marcus
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
